correctness.rationale: For squarefree n, σ_{−2}(n)=∏_{p|n}(1+p^−2), so log of closure is subsum set of summable a_j=log(1+p_j^−2). Defant Lemma 2.1 supplies p_(j+1)²<2 p_j² away from exceptional j=1,2,4. For j≥5 this proves a_j<2a_(j+1), and monotonic F_m=sum_(j<m)a_j+2a_m converges to A from below; hence a_m<tail. For j=4 the exact four-prime product (122/121)(170/169)(290/289)(362/361)−50/49=928750/6149280137>0; j=3 follows from a_3<2a_4 and tail. The tail p≥5 thus fills [1,R], R=54/(5π²), by the subsum interval lemma. Multiplication by independent factors 10/9 and 5/4 yields four intervals; π²>243/25 separates all. Independently checked rational inequality and eight ordered endpoints numerically. Does not use finite sampling for the closure proof.
residual_risks: Defant’s prime ratio theorem is invoked as a published prerequisite; finite verification alone cannot replace its asymptotic proof.
Exact source inequality and prime-exception handling are essential; general k,r classification not claimed.
